headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk: awesome-prompts is non-runnable while marker has no filesystem or network egress, so pairwise harm is mostly limited to manual content transfer.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: agent_a is a non-runnable content-writing repo, while agent_b is document-processing with no shared channel, MCP, or filesystem bridge. The only plausible pathway is manual copy-paste of prompt content from agent_a into agent_b, which is an unusual configuration and has small blast radius.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies prompt text from agent_a into agent_b inputs, injection content can influence agent_b.
IF a shared clipboard or external wrapper is introduced, the pathway becomes more direct.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate terminals or sessions.
Avoid copying raw prompt repositories into marker inputs.
Strip instructions from any text passed from agent_a to agent_b.
Use a plain-text review step before pasting content.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a has no data classes touched and no network egress; agent_b also has no read_filesystem, write_filesystem, or network egress. With no shared workspace or outbound channel, there is no plausible leakage path between them.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem is mounted outside the profiles, leakage risk would need reevaluation.
IF either agent is wrapped by an external uploader, the no-egress assumption no longer holds.
mitigations: Keep both agents offline.
Do not mount a shared workspace.
Avoid passing sensitive files between tools.
Verify wrapper code does not add upload steps.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a is content-writing and non-runnable, and agent_b cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping mutable resource or write surface, so a capability conflict is provably blocked by the profiles.
conditions: IF agent_b is replaced with a writable variant, shared-resource conflicts would need reassessment.
IF an external orchestrator grants write access, the current block no longer applies.
mitigations: Keep marker in read-only mode.
Do not grant filesystem write permissions.
Do not enable git automation.
Separate any future writable agent into its own workspace.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_a can supply prompt or content ideas, but agent_b is a document processor with no shell, browser, or filesystem write authority. Any cascade would require manual acceptance of agent_a's output, and agent_b lacks downstream action-taking power, so the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator treats agent_a output as authoritative source text for agent_b, errors can propagate into documents.
IF agent_b is later connected to an action-taking workflow, the severity increases.
mitigations: Require human review of agent_a outputs before use.
Use citations or source checks in marker outputs.
Keep agent_b out of action-taking pipelines.
Flag generated text as untrusted until verified.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles show no data classes touched, no network egress, and no stated residency, certification, or retention mismatch. With no documented regulated data flow, there is no compliance pathway to score beyond none.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into either agent, compliance must be re-evaluated.
IF residency or retention policies differ in a future deployment, the current assessment no longer applies.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents.
Document any future residency requirements.
Review retention settings before deployment.
